name: First person (walk, look, use)
pitch: Through your own eyes in a walled garden at dusk: light seven lanterns while slow shades drift toward you; a lit lantern makes a circle of light they cannot enter.
camera: first person, eyes at 1.6 m, mouse look (pointer lock)
controls: Mouse to look (click to capture, Esc to pause), WASD to walk, Shift to sprint, Space to jump, hold E (or the mouse button) to use what you look at, click or F to throw a spark. Gamepad works (right stick looks); touch has no look yet.
use_when: any game seen through the character's eyes: exploring, walking stories, light horror, puzzle rooms, collecting, escape rooms, and (with work) shooters. Levels are text maps the agent can type.
not_for: games where you see your character (third person, side-on, top-down), vehicles, flying
already_good: Raw mouse look (no smoothing), sensitivity, invert-Y, pitch clamp, gamepad right stick and bot through one input.look()
Walking that starts and stops at once, full-speed strafe, no faster diagonals, sprint with a small FOV kick
Jump with coyote time and buffering, a little air control
Capsule collision with wall sliding, step-up with smoothed eyes, sub-steps so nothing passes through at low frame rates
Head bob and footsteps by distance walked, a landing dip, all tunable to zero
Use by a forgiving cone with a prompt, a filling ring and an answer in sound and light
A held lantern that sways, bobs, dips and shows your health
Threats you can hear and see coming: a growing whisper, a heartbeat, screen-edge hints for anything behind you, a hiss before every lunge
An aimed throw with aim assist and a lock ring: the seed of a shooter
The level is a text map that builds both the meshes and the collision
